x: In the 440 yards race Michael was first, followed by two Valley men, and so the points were shared. In the Two Miles race we finished our six in the first six positions—a wonderful performance—with Carter beating Jordan in an inches finish in 9 min. 58 sec.

The 4 x 880 yards saw Michael going off first of our lads and he ran finely in setting up a lead over the other clubs. We were never in any danger and finished easy winners with Mitcham second, Epsom third, and Croydon last.
Michael, Kench and Shields have served the Club well, and Stimpson and Ball shown promise. Of the milers, Rice, Shaw and Jordan have done well.

Michael in the 440 yards, although it must be said that Mike had previously done a gruelling half in the S.A.A.L 4 x 880 yards. By winning this Southern Amateur League event we came out on top in the final placings, a result which is very gratifying when one considers the strength of the competing clubs.

The 4 x 300 yards was in the nature of a tragedy for us; for with Stroud going first, and Bennett continuing the good work, we saw Michael having a neck and neck race with the Croydon man over the third stage.

On May 25th, at the White City, was held the 4 x 220 yds. and we fielded a useful team in Kealey, Stroud, Mewes and Michael. Kealey elected to start for us, and drawing number 1 station, he was twice bumped very badly and so we lost any advantage which we might have had.

T.V.H. men were second and third, with Michael fourth, and so once again points were even between the two clubs. By the way, Ashcombe A.C. were also competing but they had the last two men in both these races.
Unfortunately, and I say that advisedly, we were without the sprinters we had been relying upon, and so our team for the 4 x 100 was Mewes, Bennet, Michael and Camkin.

Pettet, of the Police, over the half-mile stage; and then Michael further increased our lead by running a fine quarter. Les Bennett did the 220, and kept his advantage; so that when Gray went off for the final 220 he had a comfortable lead.

The 1 Mile Medley Relay saw Michael run a fine half-mile stage to give us a lead that was kept throughout. After an enjoyable afternoon, amid pleasant surroundings, the score board read : Belgrave H. 48 pts., Reading A.C. 23 pts., Ealing H. 20 pts., Ashcombe A.C. 9 pts., and Slough A.C. and A.E.C. 1 pt. each.

This was not too good from our point of view as regards point scoring, but we soon pulled up, gaining useful points when Fred White won the 880 yards, and Eddie Pack and Michael came home together in the 440 yards.

Pack, Michael, Herbert and Bird will value their bronze medals. Our team ran impressively in their heat, and in the final Eddie Pack gave our team a splendid start, unofficial watches timing him to do a shade outside 50 seconds.
